paper_metadata.title: Contextual Quantum Neural Networks for Stock Price Prediction

summary: The paper proposes a quantum multi-task learning (QMTL) architecture for predicting stock return distributions using variational quantum circuits. Experiments on S&P 500 data with context size T=3 show that QMTL reduces KL divergence compared to single-task learning (e.g., Apple: 0.1047 → 0.0614; Google: 0.1239 → 0.0754) while using fewer parameters (32 → 16). All experiments are performed on small simulated circuits (≈8 qubits) and demonstrate algorithmic feasibility rather than practical quantum advantage.

problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize fidelity loss between loaded quantum state and target contextual distribution

State preparation overhead scales exponentially with context size

experiments.description: Noise robustness study evaluating depolarizing gate noise and readout error on QMTL predictions.
key_results: KL divergence between noisy and noiseless outputs increases with noise probability from 0 to 50%.
Depolarizing noise produces faster divergence growth than readout error.
Gate noise affects computation throughout the circuit while readout noise affects only final measurement.
